B. Significant Impacts of Relocation
Every effort was made in the planning of this project to minimize the right-of-way requirements. However, a total of eight (8) structures will be affected by total acquisition in order to implement this proposal. Other buildings will be affected to the extent that overhangs will have to be removed or modified.
A total of six (6) commercial structures will be directly effected because of the highway reconstruction and widening. Of the six (6) buildings, five are highway oriented drive-in restaurants and one is an office structure.
Due to the additional facilities recently construced and opened for business, and the economic growth of existing businesses, an accurate number of people presently employed is not available. It is estimated that perhaps as many as thirty (30) people are employed in businesses that could be affected by this improvement. However, the number of people employed would not be affected because of the availability of new businesses in the area and the availability for relocation of businesses directly affected by the improvement.
Two residential structures will need to be acquired for right-of-way purposes. One of these structures is a single family house and the other is an apartment building with sixteen single family units.
No known minority will be affected by the acquisition of dwelling units. In addition, sufficient available housing within the immediate area would be available to the people displaced by this improvement. (See Appendix "H", "Lincoln Highway Area Current Real Estate Area Available and Replacement Properties Survey, Fall and Winter 1975").
In addition, other land takings of generally 8 to 25 feet for right-of-way will be required from other properties fronting on Lincoln Highway. The right-of-way requirements have been varied in several locations to avoid the necessity of impacting upon any more buildings beyond the eight structures discussed.
Right-of-way acquisition will be in accordance with the provisions of the "Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970" and subsequent directives and guidelines issued by the Federal Highway Administration.
